evidence: tracing.py:71-74 set `rebar.candidate.usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` from the response usage
search_files for `rebar.candidate.usage` across tests/ returned `(no matches)`
search_files for `input_tokens` in tests shows only fixture bodies (`"usage": {"input_tokens": 1, ...}`) in the tracing tests, never a span-attribute assertion
The happy-path test asserts only ATTR_ORDER/ATTR_MODEL/ATTR_OUTCOME (test_candidate_tracing.py final assertions), not usage keys
advisory.finding: The new candidate-span usage attributes (rebar.candidate.usage.input_tokens / output_tokens) set by _CandidateHandle.returned are asserted by no test; a regression that stopped recording per-candidate usage, or recorded a wrong/absent value, would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the happy-path test, after asserting outcomes, assert `spans[1].attrs["rebar.candidate.usage.input_tokens"] == 1` and `... .output_tokens == 1` (the values _ok_body emits).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a wrapped candidate model's base_url/label/model_id equal the underlying model's values.
evidence: tracing.py:166-178 add base_url/label/model_id overrides with the comment that WrapperModel `leaves these three base Model defaults in place, so forward them explicitly to stay fully transparent`
The tests exercise .request through a real FallbackModel but never read the wrapped model's base_url/label/model_id through the traced wrapper
advisory.finding: The three transparency-delegation properties (base_url, label, model_id) added to _TracedCandidateModel — explicitly to forward base Model defaults WrapperModel leaves in place — have no test asserting they delegate to self.wrapped, so dropping/misrouting them would not be detected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Construct wrap_candidate(m, 0, id) over a stub model with known base_url/label/model_id and assert the wrapper returns each unchanged.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the sanitized reason is non-empty (and contains the redaction/placeholder or the surviving 'boom' token) before asserting the secret is absent.
evidence: lines 214-217 only assert the secret/prompt strings are NOT in `reason`; all pass when reason == ''
tracing.py:84-85 only set `rebar.candidate.error` when `reason is not None` — so an empty/missing attribute is a reachable state the test would not flag
advisory.finding: The AC-7 sanitization test's secret-absence assertions pass vacuously when the error reason is empty: `reason = raised[0].attrs.get(ATTR_ERROR, "")` defaults to '' if the attribute was never set, so the test cannot distinguish 'sanitized' from 'error reason silently not recorded'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert reason, "the raised span must carry a (redacted) reason"` and assert a non-secret fragment such as `"boom" in reason` so the test proves the reason was populated and sanitized.
